definitions.gloss: washing the whole thing; full wash
definitions.explanation: Washing an item completely without taking it apart or spot-cleaning. Often used for large items like futons, carpets, or garments that are washed entirely rather than just having stains treated.

examples.japanese: この{布団|ふとん}は{丸洗|まるあら}いできる。
examples.english: This futon can be washed whole.

examples.japanese: コートを{丸洗|まるあら}いに{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I sent my coat out for a full wash.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{靴|くつ}が{泥|どろ}だらけになったので、{丸洗|まるあら}いした。
examples.english: The kids' shoes got covered in mud, so I gave them a full wash.

notes:
USAGE:
Used both as a noun ({丸洗|まるあら}い) and as a verb with する ({丸洗|まるあら}いする). Often appears on product labels to indicate that an item can be machine-washed whole.

WORD FORMATION:
{丸|まる} (whole, entire) + {洗|あら}い (washing). The {丸|まる} prefix means 'completely' or 'as a whole.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {丸洗|まるあら}いOK / {丸洗|まるあら}い{可|か} (machine-washable / can be fully washed)
- {布団|ふとん}の{丸洗|まるあら}い (full washing of a futon)
- {丸洗|まるあら}いに{出|だ}す (to send out for full washing)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {水洗|みずあら}い: washing with water — focuses on the method (water) rather than completeness
